{"type":"text","timestamp":1794664721666,"sessionID":"ses_e25c379fdffe5b6srDeysf5voo","part":{"id":"prt_1da5a691e001fuQQxxklIcwZPz","messageID":"msg_1da5a43b5001JVNg9bO2Ciii2P","sessionID":"ses_e25c379fdffe5b6srDeysf5voo","type":"text","text":"I've submitted **Lantern**, a 12-instruction oneshot scanner that switches to a core clear once it finds the opponent. It averages **0.437** against the 30 sparring warriors over 500 rounds each. The hidden hill score will probably be lower: its warriors are stronger, and I tuned the constants on the sparring set, so some of that 0.437 is overfitting. If the hill score did match, the reward would come out at about 0.85.\n\n```redcode\nstep    equ     3082\nhalf    equ     144\n        org     top\ngate    dat     0,      0\ntop     add.f   inc,    ptr\nptr     seq.i   3180,  3180+half\n        jmp     found\n        jmp     top\nfound   mov.ab  ptr,    gate\n        add.ab  #-5,    gate\nclr     spl     #0,     0\n        mov     bmb,    >gate\n        djn.f   -1,     >gate\nbmb     dat     <2667,  12\ninc     dat     step,   step\n```\n\nIt compares pairs of cells 144 apart, moving 3082 cells per step. At the first pair that differs, it starts a self-splitting clear just behind that spot. The clear sweeps forward through the whole core writing `dat` bombs. When the sweep wraps round and overwrites `gate`, the pointer resets past Lantern's own code, so the clear never wipes itself.\n\nHow the score was reached (sparring average, 500 rounds unless noted):\n- **Silk-style paper:** about 0.41 at its best, but it tied a lot.\n- **First oneshot (untuned):** 0.408 at 100 rounds.\n- **Random tuning of step and offsets:** about 0.418.\n- **Wider gap between the two compared cells (34 → 144):** 0.437.\n\nWhat didn't pay off:\n- **Choosing between paper and oneshot each round using p-space memory:** this was my main experiment, and it scored 0.32–0.395, below either strategy alone.\n  - It had two bugs, both now fixed. LDP needs the `.ab` modifier. Stray processes later in the round could re-run the STP instruction and corrupt the saved state.\n  - Even after the fixes, the extra code made the warrior bigger and slower to start. That cost more than the switching gained.\n- **Other changes that lowered the score:**\n  - adding an imp\n  - mixing `spl` and `dat` bombs in the clear\n  - a clear with two pointers\n  - picking which of the two scanned cells to start clearing from\n  - extra code generally\n\nMy files are in `/app/w/`; the submitted warrior is `/app/w/final.red`.","time":{"start":1794664720670,"end":1794664721665}}}
